log "Headscale: запуск"
install -d -m 755 /opt/headscale/config /opt/headscale/data
# Written every run: the file is ours, and a domain or hostname
# change has to reach it. Headscale generates its own noise key
# into the data directory on first start and never rewrites it.
cat > /opt/headscale/config/config.yaml <<'EOF_HEADSCALE'
server_url: https://mesh.example.com
listen_addr: 0.0.0.0:8080
metrics_listen_addr: 127.0.0.1:9090
noise:
  private_key_path: /var/lib/headscale/noise_private.key
prefixes:
  v4: 100.64.0.0/10
  v6: fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48
  allocation: sequential
derp:
  server:
    # The point of self-hosting: without this, a node that cannot
    # reach its peer directly falls back to Tailscale's public
    # relays. Measured — a lab node reported a relay region abroad
    # while this was off.
    enabled: true
    region_id: 999
    region_code: "gryonix"
    region_name: "mesh.example.com"
    stun_listen_addr: "0.0.0.0:3478"
    private_key_path: /var/lib/headscale/derp_server_private.key
  # No public relay map: everything stays on this host.
  urls: []
  auto_update_enabled: false
database:
  type: sqlite
  sqlite:
    path: /var/lib/headscale/db.sqlite
log:
  level: info
dns:
  magic_dns: true
  base_domain: ts.example.com
  # Service names inside the mesh, pointed at this server's own
  # mesh address. A separate FILE rather than an inline
  # `extra_records` block (the two are mutually exclusive) because
  # the addresses are not known now: a node's mesh address is
  # handed out when it joins, which is after this file is written.
  # Headscale watches the file and picks up changes without a
  # restart — measured on v0.29.3, along with the other half of
  # that behaviour: it REFUSES TO START if the path is missing,
  # which is why the empty file below is written before `up`.
  extra_records_path: /etc/headscale/extra-records.json
  nameservers:
    global:
      - 1.1.1.1
policy:
  mode: database
EOF_HEADSCALE
chmod 600 /opt/headscale/config/config.yaml
# Created only when ABSENT, unlike config.yaml: this file holds the
# published names, and rewriting it on every run would drop them on
# the next re-install.
if [ ! -f /opt/headscale/config/extra-records.json ]; then
  printf '[]\\n' > /opt/headscale/config/extra-records.json
  chmod 644 /opt/headscale/config/extra-records.json
fi
cd /opt/headscale
docker compose -p headscale pull -q
docker compose -p headscale up -d
